records.claim: The predictor maintains a 65-entry Tomasulo-like register status table tracking whether logical registers R0-R64 hold a 12-bit digest or a 14-bit tag.
records.quote: To keep track of which logical registers hold a valid digest at prediction time, RUNLTS adopts a method similar to Tomasulo's algorithm. We use a dedicated table that contains one entry per logical register. Each entry consists of a valid bit and a payload that can hold either a 14-bit tag or a 12-bit digest.
records.why: The paper specifies a dedicated Tomasulo-like table with one entry per logical register holding a valid bit and a 14-bit tag or 12-bit digest.

records.claim: Logical registers are partitioned across 8 banks, each using 3 usefulness tables (UT0-UT2) to select the most useful register to index 3 prediction weight tables (WT0-WT2).
records.quote: Figure 5(c) shows the register components, which exploit correlations between register values and branch directions. This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers. As with the SC's existing components, it comprises two tables: one that tracks prediction usefulness and one that determines the predicted branch direction.
records.why: The paper defines organizing the component into eight banks with usefulness tables selecting registers for the direction prediction tables.

records.claim: Bank weight sums are conditionally scaled by 2.5 if useful or suppressed to 0 if not, and summed into sR to be added into LSUM.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) specifies that the bank weight summation node feeds an 'x0 or x2.5' multiplier stage before entering the sR cross-bank adder.

records.claim: Value digests expire after 256 decoded instructions to prevent stale values from degrading accuracy.
records.quote: Preliminary experiments revealed that stale digests degrade prediction accuracy. Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: The paper explicitly states that each digest is invalidated after 256 subsequent instructions are decoded.

records.claim: The predictor requires writeback and completion signals from the execution unit providing destination register ID and produced value digests.
records.quote: When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: The paper specifies that upon instruction completion, the register status table payload is overwritten with the produced value digest.

records.claim: The predictor requires signals at decode notifying when an instruction writing a destination register enters the pipeline and assigning its ROB tag.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: The paper states that at decode time, instructions writing registers clear the valid bit and record their ROB index as a tag.

records.claim: The predictor interface receives notification of decoded instructions to decrement decay counters.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.

trailing one/zero #    [5:0]         6 bits  count of trailing 0s (or 1s)

  Value[5:0]             [11:6]        6 bits  the 6 LSBs of the register
records.why: Figure 6(a) transcription defines the 3-field XOR overlap structure at bit offsets 0, 3, and 6.

records.claim: Flag register digest replicates 4 condition-code bits three times into a 12-bit digest.

records.claim: Completed instructions ahead in the ROB retain valid digests across a misprediction pipeline flush recovery.
records.quote: However, we found that by the time a branch resolves and its misprediction is revealed, many in-flight instructions have already finished execution, thereby enlarging the set of values visible to the predictor when it restarts, and this fact can be exploited.
records.why: Section 4.2 explains that execution results of instructions completed before flush resolution remain available upon restart.

records.claim: The update algorithm triggers at branch commit / resolution following TAGE-SC-L operation.

records.claim: Only logical registers available at prediction time are trained, and if multiple are available in a bank, one is randomly chosen for single write-port update.
records.quote: During training, we update the correlations only for logical registers that were available at prediction time. If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update. Owing to this training method, each table in the register component also needs just a single write port.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that training updates only available registers and picks one randomly per bank to support single-write-port RAMs.

records.claim: The usefulness table entry weights are incremented when bank prediction matches actual outcome while differing from base prediction, and decremented when bank prediction is incorrect.
